extracted.intended_audience: poets, dramatists, critics, and educated readers of literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and aesthetic standards for judging or composing drama and poetry, emphasizing structural unity, moral effect, linguistic manner, character individuality, and the proper scope and means of the tragic and comic arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing satire with human kindness
rubrics_metrics.description: A central figure of beauty or tenderness in a crowd of humorous deformities 'diffuses through all, and over each of the group, a spirit of reconciliation and human kindness' and 'prevents the instructive merriment ... from degenerating into the heart-poison of contempt or hatred.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sympathetic or reconciling elements amid satire so that laughter remains instructive rather than contemptuous; use contrasts that blend tenderness with humour (example: Hogarth's central female face among humorous deformities). Anti-pattern: purely derisive satire that breeds contempt rather than humane understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensational stage devices as substitute for substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatrical tricks (explosions, real gunpowder, startling physical effects) may astonish but are superficial compared to true dramatic effect: 'a little real gunpowder being set fire to ... the naturalness of the scene was quite astonishing!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on noisy special effects or sensational staging to create dramatic impact; these are often spectacle without imaginative or moral depth. Use stagecraft to support, not replace, character, language, and moral or imaginative engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural unity: fitness of parts and harmony of the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Good drama preserves 'a fitness in the parts, and a harmony in the whole' and thus constitutes a consistent work of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that scenes, episodes, and stylistic choices cohere into a unified artistic nature. Each part should serve the whole; disjointed or merely episodic constructions weaken dramatic power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excite active thought and strive for ideal excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: A great drama 'excite[s] the minds of the spectators to active thought, to a striving after ideal excellence' rather than stupefying the audience into mere sensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to engage the intellect and imagination as well as the emotions; encourage reflection and aspiration rather than passive emotional reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate the mind within bounds of pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Tragic scenes should affect us 'within the bounds of pleasure, and in union with the activity both of our understanding and imagination' and 'transport the mind to a sense of its possible greatness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance emotional effect with intellectual and imaginative activity; the audience's pleasure should coexist with elevation and enlargement of thought, not with cheapening or mere sentimental indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pandering and maudlin pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern sentimental plays often offer 'the best Christian morality' that flatters without demanding sacrifice, 'adulation so loathsome' and 'maudlin tears of drunkenness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True moral drama requires moral cost and genuine virtue, not flattering consolations that reassure the audience's vices. Avoid scenes that solicit easy sympathy through contrived or gratuitous pathos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involution of the universal in the individual (Aristotelian principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle required 'an involution of the universal in the individual' — the poet should embody universal truths within particular characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct characters through which broad human truths are manifested concretely. Use the individual case to reveal universals; avoid abstraction divorced from vivid particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularize class-characteristics to preserve individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Class-characteristics that make characters instructive must be 'modified and particularized in each person' so that life produces a distinct sense of individuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when using stock or class-types, add specific, individualized details so characters feel like unique persons rather than mere exemplars or caricatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize manner (language, situations, passions) over mere plot novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The drama's excellence lies in 'the delightful language of the poet', the 'situations, the action and reaction of the passions' rather than merely in curiosity about the story's events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on how the story is told — style, psychological truth, scene construction — rather than treating novelty of incident as the primary value. A known plot can be profound if executed with superior manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select subject matter and heroes appropriate to tragedy's scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Tragedy derives loftiness from 'the dependence of thousands on the fate of one' and from the 'power of destiny and the controlling might of heaven' which elevate characters beyond petty concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects, stakes, and personages whose consequences and scale justify tragic treatment; petty domestic matters rarely sustain the highest tragic effects without artful enlargement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject dramatic systems that reward vice or invert natural moral order
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic denounces 'a moral and intellectual Jacobinism' in drama that confuses causes and effects and rewards criminals with public sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dramaturgy that systematically exalts vice, rewards wrongdoing, or subverts moral cause-and-effect for cheap popularity. Popular sympathy should not be bought by moral inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verse harmony: prioritize pauses, cadences, and paragraphic sweep
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonious verse consists 'in the apt arrangement of pauses and cadences, and the sweep of whole paragraphs ... and not in the even flow, much less in the prominence of antithetic vigour, of single lines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose verse with attention to long-breathed cadences and rhetorical shaping over paragraphs; use striking single lines sparingly and for deliberate effect rather than as continual emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful language and natural transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The French serious drama is criticized for 'perpetual falsification of the language, and of the connections and transitions of thought, which Nature has appropriated to states of passion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language and rhetorical transitions that truthfully represent the psychology of passion; avoid artificial phrasing and forced transitions that betray natural speech and thought.
